_meta.note: The RPG-layer half of a movement action -- the closed vocabulary MovementPayloadPolicy (FusionRpg.Core.Actions.Movement) validates against. Ids and prose only, no magnitude of any kind: the atom roll (Instantiator.Draw) owns every number this vocabulary could carry. 'channels' is 3 of the 261+ registered derived-stat channels; 'statuses' is exactly the 13 non-UnityCc status ids of StatusCatalogBootstrap.cs:16-58 (the 8 UnityCc-wrapped ones -- butter, freeze, cold, poison, hypno, ember, jala, kelp -- are refused at load, never admitted, because a UnityCc status needs the Unity CC executor and therefore the lawn, which would let a movement action pass HasStandalonePayload while being inert with the game closed); 'payloadKinds' is the closed set buff|status|tempo|none.
_meta.rebalance: A balance pass narrows the 'statuses' list by DELETING rows (the rule stays 'any non-UnityCc status'; the seeded default is every id that rule currently admits) -- never widens it past the load-time UnityCc predicate. 'channels' and 'payloadKinds' are structural, not a balance surface. Never hand-edit: use tools/tuning/publish.py movement-payload key=value (publish.py is domain-name-agnostic -- it globs data/tuning/<domain>.v*.json, so no separate registration step exists for a new domain). A new version bumps `version` and keeps this one on disk for revert.

channels.description: move.range is how far an actor may reposition (DerivedStatChannels.cs:525, FlatSum, StatClass.Pool); it is not attack reach, not movement speed, and not a duration -- and it has no production reader today (DerivedStatRegistry.cs:237 is its only registration; DominanceGuard.cs:103 reserves it), so a payload written entirely here is declared and inert until a reader lands.

skill.cooldown.movement is the movement action-category's own cooldown tempo channel (DerivedStatChannels.cs:482,485, StatClass.Race); it is never a damage or defense multiplier, never shared with attack/defense/support/status, and it has no production reader today (DerivedStatRegistry.cs:177-180, DominanceGuard.cs:118-119).

skill.effectiveness.movement is the movement action-category's own effectiveness tempo channel (DerivedStatChannels.cs:483,486, StatClass.Feeder); it is never an attack-damage multiplier, never shared with attack/defense/support/status, and it has no production reader today (DerivedStatRegistry.cs:177-180, DominanceGuard.cs:118-119).

payloadKinds.description: buff names a stat-modifying movement payload (a legal channel write); it is never a status application and never the explicit no-payload marker.
status names a status-applying movement payload (a legal status from this file's own 'statuses' list); it is never a stat modification and never the explicit no-payload marker.
tempo names a cooldown- or effectiveness-channel movement payload; it is never a stat buff outside the movement category's own tempo channels and never a status application.

none is the explicit no-payload marker a planner may state directly instead of by omission; it is never treated as a legal standalone payload, and a category=Movement action carrying only none is rejected by ActionValidator.
